hero.title: The Internet & APIs
hero.subtitle: How computers talk to each other on the internet.

lead.paragraph1: You open a website. Your computer sends a message to another computer. That computer is far away. The answer comes back in less than one second. How does this work?
lead.paragraph2: Three ideas explain this. These ideas are in every app. By the end, you will understand what happens when a web page loads.

clientServer.title: Client and Server: Like a Restaurant
clientServer.analogy: Think of a restaurant. You are the guest. You order something. The waiter brings the order to the kitchen. The kitchen makes the food. The waiter brings it back. On the internet, your computer is the guest. It is called the client. The other computer is the kitchen. It is called the server.
clientServer.scientific: The client sends a request. The server sends a response back. The web uses HTTP as its language. HTTP stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol. A request has a method like GET or POST. The response has a code like 200 or 404.
clientServer.analogyBreak: A web server serves thousands of guests at the same time. No restaurant can do that. A server can also become a client itself. The network can make mistakes. Data can get lost.

walkthrough.title: What happens when you type google.com?
walkthrough.step1: Your browser asks: What is the address of google.com?
walkthrough.step5: The server sends the web page back.
walkthrough.step6: The browser shows the page. This takes less than half a second.

misconception.title: Wrong idea: Internet is the same as the Web
misconception.text: Internet and Web are not the same. The internet is cables and routers. The Web is just one service on the internet. There is also email and streaming.

dns.title: Addresses: IP and DNS
dns.analogy: DNS is like a phone book. But not one big book. It is a chain of books. Each book knows part of the answer. In the end, you find the right number.
dns.scientific: Every device on the internet has an IP address. It is a number. IPv4 has numbers like 192.168.0.1. DNS translates names like google.com into these numbers. Ports are like extensions. Port 443 is for secure websites.

ipv4.label: IPv4 Addresses
ipv4.description: There are 4.3 billion. That is not enough for all devices.

dnsTime.label: DNS Lookup
dnsTime.description: The name lookup takes about 50 milliseconds.

dns.phoneBookAnalogy: Your browser first checks its own memory. Then it asks your internet provider. The provider asks further. In the end, the IP address comes back. The result is saved.
dns.analogyBreak: A real phone book is printed once a year. DNS entries can change in minutes. DNS queries are active requests to servers.

resolution.title: DNS Resolution: Step by Step
resolution.step2: No match: request goes to the internet provider.
resolution.step3: The provider asks the root server: Who knows .com?
resolution.step4: The .com server says: Google uses these servers.
resolution.step5: Google's server gives the IP address.
resolution.step6: The address is saved. Next time it will be faster.

dns.portsExplanation: Ports are like extensions. The IP address is the main number. The port points to the right service. Port 80 is HTTP. Port 443 is HTTPS. Port 22 is SSH.

misconception.title: Wrong idea: My IP address shows who I am
misconception.text: Your IP address changes often. Many devices share one address. The IP is like a hotel room number. It does not show who you are.

apis.title: APIs: The Menu for Programs
apis.analogy: An API is like a menu. The menu shows what is available. You order by the rules. You get your result. It does not matter if you are an app or a program.
apis.scientific: API stands for Application Programming Interface. It is an interface. One program uses the functions of another program. Web APIs use HTTP. The data comes as JSON.
apis.analogyBreak: API responses can be very complex. APIs often need a key. There are limits on requests per minute. That does not happen in a restaurant.

comparison.websiteResult: The server sends HTML with colors and images. The browser shows the page. Made for humans.
comparison.apiResult: The server sends data as JSON. A program processes the data. Made for machines.

apis.weatherExample: An example: A weather API. You send the city name Berlin. The answer comes as JSON: temperature 18 degrees, cloudy. No images. Just data.
apis.aiForwardLink: Exciting: An AI API works the same way. You send a question. The answer comes as JSON. Instead of a database, a neural network does the work.

misconception.title: Wrong idea: APIs are only for programmers
misconception.text: Every app on your phone uses APIs. The weather widget asks an API. The transit app asks an API. You do not see the APIs. But they are everywhere.

httpMethods.title: HTTP Methods and Status Codes
httpMethods.text: HTTP has a small vocabulary. GET means: read something. POST means: send something. PUT means: replace something. DELETE means: remove something.
httpMethods.statusCodes: Status codes are short answers. 200 means: all good. 404 means: not found. 500 means: the server has a problem.

aiApis.title: From Weather APIs to AI APIs
aiApis.text: A weather API: You send a city name. You get the temperature. An AI API: You send a question. You get an answer. The pattern is the same.
aiApis.samePattern: HTTP and JSON are the same in both cases. Only the server works differently. Once a database. Once a neural network.

items.clientServer: The internet follows a pattern: Client asks, server answers. This is true for websites, apps, and AI chatbots.
items.dns: DNS is the phone book of the internet. It translates names into numbers.
items.api: An API is an interface. Programs talk to other programs through it. Every app uses APIs.
items.json: JSON is the format for API data. It is easy to read. Every programming language understands JSON.
items.cloud: The cloud is computers in data centers. They work like any website.

q1.question: What does DNS do on the internet?
q1.explanation: DNS translates names like google.com into numbers. Without DNS, you would have to remember the numbers.

q2.question: You type google.com. You get an error: "DNS resolution failed." What does that mean?
q2.b: Your browser could not translate google.com into a number
q2.explanation: The browser could not translate the name google.com into an IP address. This is often because of the DNS server or the internet connection.

q3.question: A weather app shows 18 degrees for Berlin. What happens in the background?
q3.a: The app has all weather data saved
q3.c: The app asks an API and gets JSON data back
q3.d: The app takes a photo of a weather website
q3.explanation: The app asks a weather API. The API sends the temperature back as JSON data. No website. Just data.

q4.question: Websites and APIs both use HTTP. What is the difference?
q4.b: Websites use GET, APIs use POST
q4.c: Websites send HTML for the browser. APIs send JSON data for programs.
q4.explanation: Websites send HTML with images and colors. APIs send JSON data without images. Both use HTTP.

checkpoint.title: Comprehension Check
checkpoint.item1: You type google.com. But the page does not come. What does the browser do before it shows the page?
checkpoint.item2: Why does DNS exist? Why do we not just type in numbers?
checkpoint.item3: Your weather widget shows 18 degrees for Berlin. Where does the app get this number?

enrichment.sectionTitle: Try It: The Journey of a Web Request

intro.title: HTTP Request: From Browser to Server
intro.description: Click Play. Follow step by step what happens when your browser calls an API.

edu.title: Why does this matter?
edu.description:
Every website uses HTTP requests.
Every app uses HTTP requests.
Every AI tool uses HTTP requests.
When you understand how a request works,
you can use APIs.
You can find errors faster.
You understand how software communicates.

stage.desc1: You type a web address. The browser is the client. It starts the request.
stage.desc2: The browser needs a number for the name. It asks the DNS server.
stage.desc3: With the number, the browser connects to the server.
stage.desc4: The browser sends the request. It says what it wants.
stage.desc5: The server gets the request. It looks up the answer.
stage.desc6: The server sends the answer back. It includes the data.
